mainTopic: The view of the משנה on שחיטה versus stabbing (רבי עקיבא and רבי ישמעאל), רבא's reading of the three phrases of the משנה, and which knife notches make a knife unfit for שחיטה.
overview: The גמרא first finishes rejecting the idea that the משנה's words "לעולם שוחטין" follow רבי ישמעאל. Under that reading the rule would be obvious, since in exile we are even farther from the מקדש. רב יוסף explains instead that the משנה follows רבי עקיבא. In his view, בשר נחירה (stabbed meat) was allowed in the מדבר and became forbidden in ארץ ישראל, and the משנה teaches that it stays forbidden even in exile. The גמרא sums up the root disagreement: for רבי עקיבא, בשר תאוה was never forbidden, and for רבי ישמעאל, בשר נחירה was never permitted. It then tests each view against פסוקים and a משנה, and both views survive. Next, רבי ירמיה asks about stabbed meat the Jews carried into ארץ ישראל, and the question ends in תיקו. רבה points out that the three phrases of the משנה must match one another, and רבא solves this by reading all three as being about the slaughterer: who, when and where, and with what tool. Finally, the חכמים of ארץ ישראל tell שמואל's father that a notch makes a knife unfit when it tears like a saw, and the גמרא begins a new ברייתא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Exile makes meat even more obviously allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes rejecting the רבי ישמעאל explanation of the משנה. If distance from the מקדש is what permits בשר תאוה, then in exile, when we are farther away, it is surely permitted, so the משנה would have nothing to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all the more so now, when they are even farther away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is completing an argument against the earlier explanation. It says that explanation makes the משנה's rule unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי ישמעאל, בשר תאוה was allowed in ארץ ישראל because people lived far from the מקדש. Now, in exile, people are even farther away, so the permission is even stronger. A משנה would never need to teach something this obvious, so this cannot be what "לעולם שוחטין" means.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so (an "if this, then surely that" argument)
Ordinary meat eaten for enjoyment, not as a קרבן

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new idea. It is the end of an argument that started before this section, against explaining the משנה through רבי ישמעאל.

phrases.english: and all the more so now
phrases.notes: "Now" means now, in exile, after the מקדש was destroyed.

phrases.english: when they have become even more distant.
phrases.notes: More distant from the place of the מקדש, so meat should be even more clearly allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן הַשְׁתָּא דְּאַרְחִיקוּ לְהוּ טְפֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rejection of the earlier explanation (from before this section) that tied the משנה to רבי ישמעאל.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole idea that "לעולם שוחטין" reflects רבי ישמעאל's view about בשר תאוה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Under that reading, the משנה's rule would be obvious, since exile means even greater distance from the מקדש.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the משנה follows רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the משנה follows רבי עקיבא. A ברייתא shows that רבי עקיבא reads the פסוק about living far from the מקדש as forbidding meat killed by stabbing (בשר נחירה). Such meat had been allowed in the מדבר, and it became forbidden once the Jews entered ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף said: This is רבי עקיבא's view. A ברייתא teaches on the פסוק "If the place that ה׳ your God chooses to put His name there is far from you, then you shall slaughter from your cattle and your sheep" that רבי עקיבא says: the פסוק only came to forbid stabbed meat. At first stabbed meat was allowed to them, but once they entered the Land, stabbed meat became forbidden to them.
steps.whatsHappening: After the first explanation fell apart, רב יוסף gives a new explanation of the משנה. He builds it on רבי עקיבא's reading of a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, the key word in the פסוק is "וזבחת" (you shall slaughter). It means proper שחיטה became required in ארץ ישראל. Before that, in the מדבר, killing an animal by stabbing (נחירה) was enough to eat its meat.

keyTerms.meaning: Meat of an animal killed by stabbing instead of by proper שחיטה
"And you shall slaughter", the word in the פסוק requiring שחיטה
The פסוק came only to teach...

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up how the משנה's "לעולם שוחטין" can teach something new, which the earlier explanation could not do.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yosef said:
It is Rabbi Akiva, as it is taught:
phrases.notes: He means the משנה's words "one must always slaughter" follow רבי עקיבא's view.

phrases.english: "If the place is too far from you
which the Lord your God will choose
to put His name there
then you shall slaughter from your cattle and your sheep,"
Rabbi Akiva says:
the verse came only
to forbid to them the meat of stabbing,
for at first, the meat of stabbing was permitted to them,
phrases.notes: "At first" means during the years in the מדבר.

phrases.english: once they entered the Land
the meat of stabbing became forbidden to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected רבי ישמעאל explanation with one based on רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the משנה to a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think the משנה follows רבי ישמעאל and is about בשר תאוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי עקיבא and is about whether בשר נחירה is forbidden.

steps.title: Why the משנה says "always slaughter"
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף finishes his explanation. One might think that after the exile, stabbed meat would become allowed again, as it was in the מדבר. So the משנה teaches "לעולם שוחטין": שחיטה is always required.
steps.simpleTranslation: And now that they went into exile, one might think they return to their original permission. That is why we learned: one must always slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף now connects רבי עקיבא's view to the words of the משנה. This shows that "always" teaches something real.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the ban on stabbed meat began when the Jews entered ארץ ישראל, someone might think it ends when they leave ארץ ישראל in exile. The word "לעולם" (always) blocks that mistake: שחיטה stays required forever, in every place and every era.

keyTerms.meaning: One must always slaughter (the משנה's words)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב יוסף, "לעולם שוחטין" means שחיטה is required even in exile. Stabbed meat does not go back to being allowed the way it was in the מדבר.

phrases.english: And now that they have been exiled,
might one think they return to their original permission?
Therefore we learned: one always slaughters.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַכְשָׁיו שֶׁגָּלוּ, יָכוֹל יַחְזְרוּ לְהֶתֵּירָן הָרִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי עקיבא's view from the ברייתא to the exact words of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the משנה's word "always" teaches a real point
steps.terutzHavaAmina: After the exile, stabbed meat might become allowed again.
steps.terutzMaskana: שחיטה is required forever, so stabbed meat stays forbidden.

steps.title: What is the root disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what basic point רבי עקיבא and רבי ישמעאל really disagree about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks for the core issue behind the two views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each תנא read the same פסוק differently. The גמרא wants to state, in one line each, the basic idea that separates them.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back from the משנה to compare the two תנאים directly.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The basic point of disagreement between רבי עקיבא and רבי ישמעאל.

steps.title: Two different starting points
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא holds that בשר תאוה was never forbidden, even in the מדבר. רבי ישמעאל holds that בשר נחירה was never permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא holds: meat of desire was never forbidden at all. רבי ישמעאל holds: meat of stabbing was never permitted at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by giving each תנא's basic position in one short line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, ordinary meat was always allowed; what changed in ארץ ישראל was the requirement of שחיטה. For רבי ישמעאל, שחיטה was always required; what changed in ארץ ישראל was permission to eat ordinary meat that was not a קרבן.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא: בשר תאוה was always allowed, and בשר נחירה became forbidden in ארץ ישראל. רבי ישמעאל: בשר נחירה was always forbidden, and בשר תאוה became allowed in ארץ ישראל.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix them up. Each one treats a different thing as having changed when the Jews entered the Land.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva holds:
meat of desire was never forbidden at all,
Rabbi Yishmael holds:
meat of stabbing was never permitted at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא סָבַר: בְּשַׂר תַּאֲוָה לָא אִיתְּסַר כְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי עקיבא: בשר תאוה was never forbidden. רבי ישמעאל: בשר נחירה was never permitted.

steps.title: Challenge from the פסוק about slaughtering a קרבן
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says a קרבן in the מדבר was slaughtered. That fits רבי ישמעאל, but why would רבי עקיבא need שחיטה there?
steps.simpleTranslation: This is easy for רבי ישמעאל: the פסוק says 'and he shall slaughter the young bull.' But for רבי עקיבא, why does it say 'slaughter'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a series of challenges to רבי עקיבא. Here it uses a פסוק that says a קרבן in the מדבר was slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי ישמעאל, שחיטה was always required, so the פסוק is no surprise. For רבי עקיבא, stabbing was allowed in the מדבר, so it seems strange that the תורה demands שחיטה here.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / this works fine. It opens a contrast: one view fits, the other seems not to.
But. It brings in the side that has a problem.
A young bull, here brought as a קרבן

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Yishmael,
this is why it is written:
"And he shall slaughter the young bull."
But according to Rabbi Akiva,
what is the point of "and he shall slaughter"?

steps.triggerLanguage: בשלמא לרבי ישמעאל היינו דכתיב ושחט את בן הבקר אלא לרבי עקיבא מאי ושחט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רבי עקיבא's view from step 5 against a פסוק
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's view that בשר נחירה was allowed in the מדבר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק set in the מדבר requires שחיטה, which suggests stabbing was not enough.

steps.title: קרבנות are a special case
steps.stepSummary: קדשים are different. They always needed שחיטה, even when ordinary meat did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Holy animals are different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי עקיבא. The פסוק is about a קרבן, and קרבנות have their own rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא only said that ordinary meat (בשר תאוה) could be eaten after stabbing in the מדבר. A קרבן always required שחיטה, so the פסוק teaches nothing about ordinary meat.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary, non-holy animals. This is the group the dispute is really about.

phrases.english: Sacrificial animals are different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a different category (קדשים, not חולין)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to show that all meat in the מדבר needed שחיטה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only קרבנות needed שחיטה. Ordinary meat could be stabbed, as רבי עקיבא says.

steps.title: Challenge from the פסוק 'Will flocks and herds be slaughtered for them'
steps.stepSummary: In the story of the meat in the מדבר, the פסוק uses the word 'slaughtered.' That fits רבי ישמעאל, but for רבי עקיבא it should have said 'stabbed.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This is easy for רבי ישמעאל: it says 'Will flocks and herds be slaughtered for them?' But for רבי עקיבא, why say that? It should have said 'be stabbed for them'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge to רבי עקיבא. This פסוק speaks about ordinary meat in the מדבר, so the earlier answer about קרבנות cannot help.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק talks about food for the people, not a קרבן, and still uses the word for slaughtering. If stabbing was allowed and was the easy way, the תורה should have said 'stabbed.'

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Yishmael,
this is why it is written:
"Will flocks and herds be slaughtered for them?"
But according to Rabbi Akiva,
what is the point of "Will flocks and herds be slaughtered for them"?
It should have said "be stabbed for them"!

steps.triggerLanguage: בשלמא לרבי ישמעאל היינו דכתיב הצאן ובקר ישחט להם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge that the answer of step 7 cannot handle, because this פסוק is about ordinary meat
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's view that בשר נחירה was allowed in the מדבר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'slaughtered' is used for ordinary meat in the מדבר. That suggests שחיטה was the normal requirement.

steps.title: For them, stabbing counted as their slaughter
steps.stepSummary: In the מדבר, stabbing was their way of preparing meat, so the פסוק can call it 'slaughtering.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Their stabbing is their slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי עקיבא. The word 'slaughter' in the פסוק simply means whatever way they prepared the meat, which back then was stabbing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ישחט' here is a general word for preparing an animal to eat, not the technical שחיטה. Since stabbing was the allowed way in the מדבר, the פסוק can describe it as 'slaughtering.'

keyTerms.meaning: Killing an animal by stabbing, not by proper שחיטה
Their slaughter, meaning their accepted way of preparing meat

phrases.english: Their stabbing — that is their slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ישחט' was taken to mean real שחיטה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'ישחט' means their way of preparing meat, and in the מדבר that was stabbing.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה about covering the blood
steps.stepSummary: A משנה says that someone who stabs an animal does not have to cover its blood. That fits רבי ישמעאל, but for רבי עקיבא stabbing was once a valid way to kill, so why no כיסוי הדם?
steps.simpleTranslation: This is easy for רבי ישמעאל, as we learned: one who slaughters and the animal became a נבלה in his hand, and one who stabs, and one who tears out the סימנים, does not have to cover the blood. But for רבי עקיבא, why is he exempt from covering?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third challenge, this time from a משנה about the מצוה of covering the blood of a wild animal or bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood is covered only when the animal was killed in a valid way. For רבי ישמעאל, stabbing was never valid, so there is no covering. For רבי עקיבא, stabbing was valid in the מדבר, when this מצוה was given, so it seems stabbing should require covering.

keyTerms.meaning: It became a נבלה, an animal not killed properly
One who tears the סימנים out of place, which ruins the שחיטה
The מצוה to cover the blood of a wild animal or bird after שחיטה

steps.confusionAlert: This משנה does not say stabbing is forbidden. It says stabbing does not create the obligation to cover the blood. The challenge is that, for רבי עקיבא, stabbing once counted as a valid way to kill.

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Yishmael,
this is why we learned in a mishna:
phrases.notes: This משנה appears later in חולין, at 85a.

phrases.english: one who slaughters and it became a carcass in his hand,
and one who stabs, and one who tears out the simanim,
is exempt from covering the blood.
But according to Rabbi Akiva,
why is he exempt from covering the blood?

steps.triggerLanguage: בשלמא לרבי ישמעאל היינו דתנן השוחט ונתנבלה בידו והנוחר והמעקר פטור מלכסות
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third challenge to רבי עקיבא, now from a משנה instead of a פסוק
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's view that נחירה was a valid way to kill in the מדבר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If stabbing was once valid, it should create the obligation of כיסוי הדם. Yet the משנה exempts it.

steps.title: Once stabbing became forbidden, it stayed forbidden
steps.stepSummary: Since בשר נחירה was later forbidden, it lost its status as a valid way to kill, so it no longer requires covering the blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it became forbidden, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי עקיבא. Stabbing was valid only in the מדבר, and it stopped counting once it became forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives the law as it stands now, after the Jews entered ארץ ישראל. At that point stabbing became forbidden for good, as step 3 explained. So today stabbing is not a valid killing, and there is no כיסוי הדם.
steps.whatToRemember: All three challenges fit רבי ישמעאל easily, but רבי עקיבא survives each one: a קרבן is different, 'slaughter' in the פסוק means their way of preparing meat, and once stabbing became forbidden it stayed forbidden.

phrases.english: Since it became forbidden, it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: Stabbing became forbidden once the Jews entered ארץ ישראל, and it never went back to being allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 10 and closes the series of challenges
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because stabbing was once valid, it should still require כיסוי הדם.
steps.terutzMaskana: Stabbing lost its validity once it was forbidden, so it does not require כיסוי הדם.

steps.title: How could the gazelle and deer be permitted according to רבי ישמעאל?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says to eat ordinary meat 'like the צבי and איל.' This fits רבי עקיבא, but for רבי ישמעאל, how were the צבי and איל themselves ever permitted?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for רבי עקיבא, who says בשר תאוה was never forbidden. That is why the פסוק says: 'Just as the gazelle and the deer are eaten, so shall you eat it.' But for רבי ישמעאל, who says בשר תאוה was forbidden in the מדבר, were the gazelle and deer themselves allowed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge against רבי ישמעאל from a פסוק. The פסוק uses the צבי and איל as an example of meat that was already allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק tells the Jews that in ארץ ישראל they may eat ordinary meat the same way they already eat צבי and איל. That only works if צבי and איל were already allowed in the מדבר. For רבי ישמעאל, all בשר תאוה was banned in the מדבר, so the comparison seems to point to something that was forbidden too.

keyTerms.meaning: Meat eaten just because one wants meat, not as part of a קרבן
Granted / it makes sense (sets up a contrast with 'but according to...')

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Akiva,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר בְּשַׂר תַּאֲוָה לָא אִיתְּסַר כְּלָל –
phrases.english: who says that the meat of desire was never forbidden at all,
phrases.notes: 'Meat of desire' means regular meat you eat because you want it, not from a קרבן.

phrases.english: that is what is written:
"However, as the gazelle is eaten
and the deer, so shall you eat it,"
But according to Rabbi Yishmael,

phrases.aramaic: צְבִי וְאַיָּל גּוּפֵיהּ מִי הֲוֵי שְׁרֵי?
phrases.english: were the gazelle and the deer themselves permitted?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another challenge in the same back-and-forth testing the two opinions against פסוקים.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's view that בשר תאוה was forbidden in the מדבר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק uses צבי and איל as a model of meat that was already allowed. Under רבי ישמעאל, all non-קרבן meat was forbidden, so the model seems not to exist.

steps.title: The ban only covered animals fit for a קרבן
steps.stepSummary: The ban on בשר תאוה in the מדבר applied only to domestic animals that can be brought as a קרבן. Wild animals like the צבי and איל were never included.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the תורה forbade it, it forbade only a domesticated animal that is fit to be brought as a קרבן. But a wild animal, which is not fit for a קרבן, the תורה did not forbid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about רבי ישמעאל. The ban in the מדבר only covered בהמה, not חיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי ישמעאל, the reason ordinary meat was banned was that a בהמה could have been brought as a קרבן. A צבי or איל is a חיה and can never be a קרבן, so it stayed permitted. That is why the פסוק can use them as a model of meat that was already allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Merciful One', a name for ה׳ when quoting what the Torah commands

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי ישמעאל, the ban on בשר תאוה in the מדבר covered only בהמה that could be a קרבן. Wild animals were always allowed.

phrases.english: When the Merciful One forbade it,
it was a domesticated animal that is fit to be offered,
but an undomesticated animal that is not fit to be offered,
the Merciful One did not forbid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the ban
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ישמעאל's ban covered all non-קרבן meat, including wild animals.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban covered only בהמה fit for a קרבן. צבי and איל were always allowed, so the פסוק can use them as a model.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה asks about stabbed meat brought into the land
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks what the status is of pieces of בשר נחירה that the Jews carried with them from the מדבר into ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: Pieces of stabbed meat that the Jews brought with them into the land, what is their status?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. רבי ירמיה wants to know whether בשר נחירה that was allowed in the מדבר stays allowed after entering ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 said that בשר נחירה was later forbidden. Now the question is about meat that was stabbed while it was still allowed and then brought into the land. Does its earlier permitted status carry over, or does the new ban apply to it too?

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (introduces a real open question)
Meat of an animal killed by stabbing instead of שחיטה

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:
Limbs of stabbed meat
that the Jewish people brought with them into the land,
what is their status?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 11's point that stabbed meat was later forbidden, and asks about meat caught between the two periods.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether stabbed meat prepared while it was allowed stays permitted after the Jews entered ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Which time period is the question about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks when רבי ירמיה means. During the seven years of conquest the question cannot arise, because even pork was allowed then, so stabbed meat surely was.
steps.simpleTranslation: When does the question apply? If you say during the seven years of conquest, then even non-kosher things were allowed to them, as it says: 'and houses full of all good things.' And רבי ירמיה בר אבא said in the name of רב: this includes cuts of pork. So is there any question about stabbed meat?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which time period רבי ירמיה means. It rules out the first option, the seven years of conquest, setting up the next possibility.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the conquest, the Jews were allowed to eat whatever they found in the houses, even pork, based on the פסוק 'houses full of all good things.' If pork was allowed, stabbed meat from a kosher animal was surely allowed too. So רבי ירמיה must be asking about a different time.

keyTerms.meaning: When? (asks what time period is meant)
If you say (introduces an option the גמרא will reject)
The seven years the Jews spent conquering ארץ ישראל
Is it even a question? (it is obvious)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying pork is generally allowed. It was only allowed as spoils during the seven years of conquest.

phrases.english: When?
If you say during the seven years in which they conquered the land,
now, if even a non-kosher thing was permitted to them,
as it is written: "and houses full of all good things,"

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said in the name of Rav:
this includes cuts of pork,
phrases.notes: He means the pork they found hanging in the houses they captured was allowed to them.

phrases.english: is stabbed meat even a question?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies רבי ירמיה's question from step 14 by testing which time period he means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which time period רבי ירמיה's question is about, since during the conquest the answer would be obvious.

steps.title: The question is about the time after the conquest
steps.stepSummary: Since the question can't be about the seven years of conquest, רבי ירמיה must be asking about the years after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he is asking about the time after that.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question from step 15. רבי ירמיה is asking about the period after the seven years of conquest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the conquest, even forbidden food was allowed, so there was nothing to ask. After the conquest that permission ended. So the question is whether leftover בשר נחירה from the מדבר was still allowed then.

keyTerms.meaning: after this (after the seven years of conquest)

phrases.english: Rather, it is about the time after that.
phrases.notes: After the seven years of conquering ארץ ישראל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'when?' question raised in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The question is about the period after the seven years of conquest.

steps.title: Or the question is about the seven years after all
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: maybe the question really is about the seven years. The permission then might have covered only food taken from the גוים, not the Jews' own forbidden meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: really, he is asking about the seven years when they conquered the land. When forbidden food was allowed to them, that was the spoils of the גוים. Their own forbidden food was not allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second way to understand רבי ירמיה. He could be asking about the seven years of conquest after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 assumed that if pork was allowed during the conquest, then surely בשר נחירה was too. This answer questions that idea. Maybe the permission covered only spoils taken from the גוים, and not meat the Jews already owned and brought with them from the מדבר.

keyTerms.meaning: and if you want, say (introduces another answer)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not take back the idea that forbidden food was allowed during the conquest. It only limits that permission to food taken from the גוים.

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
really, it is about the seven years when they conquered,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אִשְׁתְּרִי לְהוּ שָׁלָל שֶׁל גּוֹיִם –
phrases.english: when it was allowed to them, it was the spoils of the gentiles;
their own was not allowed.
phrases.notes: Their own forbidden meat, like the בשר נחירה they brought from the מדבר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer that pushes back on the assumption in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The question can be about the seven years, because the permission may have covered only spoils taken from the גוים.

steps.title: The question stays unresolved
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה's question is left without an answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: The question stands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the discussion with no answer. רבי ירמיה's question remains open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source settles whether the leftover בשר נחירה was allowed. So the גמרא closes with תיקו, the word it uses for an unanswered question.

keyTerms.meaning: let it stand; the question is left unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ירמיה asked about בשר נחירה brought from the מדבר into ארץ ישראל. It is either about the years after the conquest, or about the seven years if only spoils of the גוים were allowed then. Either way, it ends in תיקו.

phrases.english: It stands unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question of רבי ירמיה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The status of the carried-over בשר נחירה is left undecided.

steps.title: How do we explain the phrase 'בכל שוחטין'?
steps.stepSummary: רבה asks: you explained the first two phrases of the משנה, so how will you explain the third one, 'בכל שוחטין'?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: you explained 'הכל שוחטין' and 'לעולם שוחטין'. How do you explain 'בכל שוחטין'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה opens a new topic. He asks how to fit the third phrase of the משנה into the explanation already given for the first two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the first two phrases were explained as being about the animals that get slaughtered. The first phrase was read to include birds. The second was read as saying meat can only be eaten through שחיטה. Now רבה asks how 'בכל שוחטין' fits that same pattern.

keyTerms.meaning: one may slaughter with anything (any cutting tool)

phrases.english: Rabba said:
You explained 'all slaughter' and 'one may always slaughter';
'one slaughters with anything' – how do you explain it?

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁנֵּית ״הַכֹּל שׁוֹחֲטִין״ וּ״לְעוֹלָם שׁוֹחֲטִין״, ״בַּכֹּל שׁוֹחֲטִים״ – מַאי מְשַׁנֵּית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about how to read the three phrases of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the third phrase can be explained the same way as the first two.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier readings of "הכל שוחטין" and "לעולם שוחטין" as being about the animals that are slaughtered (נשחטין).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The three phrases of the משנה are parallel. If the first two are about the animals, there is no matching way to read "בכל שוחטין", which is about tools (step 20 spells this out).

steps.title: The tools reading doesn't match the other two phrases
steps.stepSummary: You can't simply say it means flint, glass, or reed. The three phrases must all be about the same subject: either all about the slaughterer or all about the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say it means flint, glass, or the stalk of a reed, isn't it taught like the other phrases? If those are about the people who slaughter, this one should be too. If those are about the animals that are slaughtered, this one should be too.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה blocks the obvious answer before anyone gives it. The phrases are listed together, so they should all be about the same subject.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two phrases were explained as being about the animals (נשחטין). 'Which tools' is about how the person slaughters, not about the animal. So the earlier explanations leave this third phrase not matching the others.

phrases.english: And if you say,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בְּצוֹר בֵּין בִּזְכוּכִית בֵּין בִּקְרוּמִית שֶׁל קָנֶה,
phrases.english: whether with flint, whether with glass, whether with the stalk of a reed,
but isn't it taught like those others?
If those are about the ones who slaughter,
this too is about the ones who slaughter;
and if those are about the ones that are slaughtered,
this too is about the ones that are slaughtered.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא, בֵּין בְּצוֹר בֵּין בִּזְכוּכִית בֵּין בִּקְרוּמִית שֶׁל קָנֶה, הָא דּוּמְיָא דְּהָנָךְ קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the obvious answer to רבה's question.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The plain 'tools' reading, when the first two phrases are read as being about the animals.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The three phrases must all be about the same subject, and here they would not be.

steps.title: רבא: all three phrases are about the person slaughtering
steps.stepSummary: רבא rereads the whole משנה as being about the slaughterer. 'הכל שוחטין' includes a כותי and a ישראל משומד. 'לעולם שוחטין' means at any time and in any place. 'בכל שוחטין' means with flint, glass, or reed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: 'all slaughter' appears twice; one time includes a כותי, and one time includes a ישראל משומד. 'One may always slaughter' means by day or by night, on a rooftop or on top of a ship. 'One slaughters with anything' means with flint, glass, or the stalk of a reed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא solves the problem by changing how the first two phrases are read. Now all three phrases are about the person who slaughters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once 'הכל' means 'everyone' and 'לעולם' means 'at any time or place', all three phrases are about the slaughterer: who, when and where, and with what. 'הכל שוחטין' appears in two different משניות, so each one adds a different kind of person. Rooftops and ships are allowed even though someone might think it looks like serving the stars or the sea.

keyTerms.meaning: a Jew who breaks the Torah's laws
the sharp outer stalk of a reed

steps.whatToRemember: In רבא's reading, 'הכל, לעולם, בכל' answer three questions about the slaughterer: who, when and where, and with what.
steps.whyThisMatters: It makes the משנה read the same way all the way through, and it tells us which people, times, places, and tools are valid for שחיטה.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
'All slaughter':
one is to include a Samaritan,
and one is to include a Jewish transgressor.
'One may always slaughter':
whether by day or by night,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בְּרֹאשׁ הַגָּג בֵּין בְּרֹאשׁ הַסְּפִינָה.
phrases.english: whether on a rooftop or on top of a ship.
'One slaughters with anything':

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בְּצוֹר, בֵּין בִּזְכוּכִית, בֵּין בִּקְרוּמִית שֶׁל קָנֶה.
phrases.english: whether with flint, with glass, or with the stalk of a reed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: ״הַכֹּל שׁוֹחֲטִין״, חֲדָא לְאֵתוֹיֵי כּוּתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Solves the mismatch from step 20 by reading all three phrases as being about the slaughterer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first two phrases were about the animals, so the 'tools' phrase did not fit with them.
steps.terutzMaskana: All three phrases are about the slaughterer: who, when and where, and with what.

steps.title: The משנה excludes the harvest sickle and the saw
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the last words of the משנה: you may slaughter with anything except a מגל קציר and a מגירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Except for a harvest sickle and a saw.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the final words of the משנה. It is setting up a discussion of which cutting tools are not allowed for שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 explained 'בכל שוחטין' as 'you may slaughter with flint, glass, or reed.' Now the גמרא looks at the exception to that rule. A sickle and a saw have teeth, and teeth tear instead of cutting cleanly.

keyTerms.meaning: A harvest sickle, which has a jagged, toothed edge

phrases.english: Except for a harvest sickle and the saw.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining 'בכל שוחטין', the גמרא moves to the exception in the same line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Toothed tools like a harvest sickle or a saw may not be used for שחיטה.

steps.title: שמואל's father sends notched knives to ask about them
steps.stepSummary: אבוה דשמואל kept making notches in knives and sending them to ארץ ישראל to find out which notches make a knife unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל's father would make a notch in a knife and send it, then make another notch and send it again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells how אבוה דשמואל asked a practical question. He sent real knives with different kinds of notches to the חכמים in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules out a saw, but it does not say what to do with a regular knife that has a small nick in it. אבוה דשמואל wanted to know exactly which kind of פגם ruins a knife. He sent several samples to find the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He made a notch or nick (in the knife's edge)

phrases.english: Shmuel's father
notched (a knife) and sent it,
phrases.notes: He sent it to the חכמים in ארץ ישראל to ask if it could be used for שחיטה.

phrases.english: notched (another way) and sent it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the משנה's exclusion of the saw to ask about a knife that has a notch.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which kind of notch in a knife makes it unfit for שחיטה?

steps.title: The answer: a notch is a problem when it works like a saw
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים of ארץ ישראל replied with a general rule: 'We learned like a saw.' A notch that tears the way a saw does makes the knife unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent back to him: we learned that it is like a saw.
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of judging each knife one by one, the חכמים gave אבוה דשמואל one rule that covers every case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer ties the notch question back to the word מגירה in the משנה. A notch is a problem when it catches and tears, the way the teeth of a saw tear back and forth. So the משנה's 'saw' becomes the measure for judging any notch.
steps.whatToRemember: A notch disqualifies a knife when it acts like a saw, tearing the סימנים instead of cutting them smoothly.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a practical test for checking a שחיטה knife: the question is whether a nick would tear the way a saw does.

phrases.english: They sent to him:
We learned: like a saw.
phrases.notes: They mean that the משנה's word 'saw' is the test. A notch that tears like a saw's teeth is not allowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אבוה דשמואל's question from the previous step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A notch disqualifies the knife when it acts like a saw.

steps.title: Opening a new teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to quote a ברייתא, a teaching of the חכמים from outside the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to bring a ברייתא, and the teaching itself comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These words only introduce a new source. The actual teaching continues after this part of the text.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the time of the משנה that was not put into the משנה

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the notch question is settled, the גמרא introduces a new ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces a ברייתא whose content follows.
